title: Give the route an identity so a finished feature's lane stops floor-setting the next one
action: The route object is {class, lane, flags, product_files, rationale, updated_at} stored under the "route" key of whichever record is active (workflows.rs:776-778) — it carries no feature identity. start_default (policy.rs:415-517) reads the WHOLE prior record with read_state_strict and inserts only feature/mode/phase/approved_gates/summary/next_action before writing it back, so the previous feature's route rides along untouched; start_lane (policy.rs:384-409) does not have this problem because it builds a fresh Map. Then run_route hands that stale route to validate_route_lane_transition (workflows.rs:761), which compares lane against lane with no idea whose feature it belonged to, and refuses: 'route --set: refused — the feature's route is lane "high-risk" and lane "small" would move it off high-risk; rule violated: high-risk lanes never demote.' Measured live: after `bee state start-feature --feature feature-swap-door`, route --show still returned worktree-reclaim's route (lane high-risk, files 7, updated_at 2026-08-05T10:07:35Z), and two one-file bugfixes had to run under a high-risk label they never earned. Three changes, all small: (1) start_default removes the "route" key from the record it writes — a feature that has not been triaged has no route, which is exactly the state `cells claim`'s no-route warning (cells/handlers_write.rs:988-997) exists to detect. Touch nothing else it carries. (2) validate_route_set_flags (workflows.rs:486-583) stamps the route with the feature it was recorded for, so identity travels with the record from now on. (3) run_route (workflows.rs:761) only runs the transition check when the existing route's feature MATCHES the record's current feature; a route belonging to another feature — or a pre-fix route with no feature field at all — is treated as no route: first-time set, no demote check, overwritten cleanly. Do NOT change validate_route_lane_transition's own signature or lane-vs-lane semantics — its seven tests (state_group/tests.rs:1494-1630) must stay green as they are; the attribution check belongs at the call site.

truths: After bee state start-feature, the record carries no route at all — route --show reads null and the first route --set for the new feature is accepted whatever its lane
A route recorded through route --set carries the feature it was triaged for
A pre-fix route with no feature field, or one naming a different feature, is treated as no route: the set is accepted and overwrites it, with no demote refusal
Within one feature the never-demote rule is unchanged — a same-feature high-risk route still refuses a demotion, and the first-demotion/demoted_at history still behaves as its existing tests assert
The lane path (start_lane and lane records) is unaffected

artifacts.substantive: start_default removes the route key before writing; no TODO stubs
the route object carries its feature, and run_route only validates a transition against a route of the same feature
tests drive start_default then route --set end to end, including a stale foreign route and a pre-fix route with no feature field

key_links: validate_route_lane_transition keeps its signature and its seven existing tests
cells claim's no-route warning is what a freshly started feature should now trigger

decisions: The never-demote rule is right within one feature and meaningless across a feature boundary (decision 132362c7, 2026-08-06)

trace.outcome: Route now carries the feature it was recorded for; start_default drops a stale route; run_route only checks demotion against a same-feature route
